teacherSummary.text: Blind and old, Oedipus arrives with Antigone at a grove near Athens. A local man tells him it is holy ground of the Eumenides and that he must leave. Oedipus refuses: Apollo foretold that he would end his days here, a blessing to his hosts and a curse to the land that cast him out.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “Child of an old blind sire, Antigone, / What region, say, whose city have we reached?” slowly and put it in my own words: Blind and old, Oedipus asks his daughter Antigone what land and whose city they have come to. Next, craft. I notice the opening line names his blindness and his dependence on her before he names anything else. The strongest word is “blind”: the man who once saw clearly and knew nothing now sees nothing and will come to know much. Then, effect. Why does the play open with Oedipus asking where he is? My answer: The play opens with Oedipus asking where he is because the king who once answered the Sphinx now needs his daughter to answer even this; finding the right place, the grove Apollo promised (lines 91–93), is what the play is about.

hsSophomore.note: Require a quotation and an explanation; push evaluative answers to address a counterclaim.

hsJunior.note: Emphasize structure and ambiguity; students should name where the text leaves matters open.

hsSenior.note: Weigh competing interpretations; students should defend the stronger reading.

ap.note: Treat each evaluative item as a thesis rehearsal: defensible claim, purposeful evidence, commentary on choices.

collegeFreshman.note: Add the extension: connect answers to historical context and one secondary perspective.

collegeSophomore.note: Use the extensions: genre and period conventions, and a published critic.

collegeJunior.note: Use the extensions: name a critical method and test it against the passage.

collegeSenior.note: Use the extensions: connect the scene to the whole work and the scholarship.

graduate.note: Use the extensions: position answers in a critical conversation and the textual history.
